rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance (proposed SDMC Div. 11)
rules.requirement: Proposed ordinance would make it unlawful for any person to sell, license or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord (§ 98.1103(a)). It would also make it unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels (§ 98.1103(b)). An algorithmic device is software that uses algorithms on nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rents or occupancy levels for San Diego residential rental property. Each month of violation, and each property where a device is used, is a separate violation. Tenants may sue a landlord for injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties, and a prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees. Remedies are cumulative.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees; takes effect on the 30th day after final passage

coverage.summary: Applies citywide in San Diego to landlords and to any person who sells, licenses or provides algorithmic devices to landlords, for residential rental property. Landlord and residential rental property are defined by reference to SDMC § 98.0702. No unit-count or construction-date limits are stated.
coverage.other_conditions: Covers only software that uses nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rents or occupancy levels.

rules.exemptions: Excluded from 'algorithmic device': (a) software used to publish reports on rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from publicly available information, that does not recommend rates or occupancy for future leases or renewals; (b) software used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.effective_date_note: Ordinance number and date of final passage are blank in the document. The effective date depends on the final passage date.

effective_date_formula.verbatim: This Ordinance will take effect and be in force on the thirtieth day from and after its final passage.

citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.review_note: The document contains only a February 2025 staff report and the draft ordinance with a blank number and passage date. Adoption cannot be confirmed from it, so the status is pending as of the 2026-10-01 query date. Check the City Clerk records for adoption.
rules.source_notes: Official city staff report, draft ordinance, City Attorney digest and strikeout version. The report notes San Francisco and Philadelphia adopted similar bans.

no_rule_findings.finding: On Oct 30, 2024 the Rules Committee voted 4-1 to ask the City Attorney to draft an ordinance banning the sale and use of price-fixing software. This is a committee action and does not itself create a rule.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: On October 30, 2024, the Rules Committee voted 4-1 to request the City Attorney’s Office work with the Council District 9 Office on drafting an ordinance banning the sale and use of price fixing software and bring the proposed ordinance to the City Council.

result.doc_summary: Staff report from Council District 9 (Feb 27, 2025) and the draft text of San Diego ordinance O-2025-107. The ordinance would add SDMC ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11 (§§ 98.1101-98.1104). It would ban selling, licensing or using algorithmic rent-setting software that relies on nonpublic competitor data. It exempts aggregated public or stale-data reports and affordable-housing program tools. Tenants could sue for injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees. It would take effect 30 days after final passage. The document shows no passage date, so it is treated as pending.
